issues.failure_explanation: The paper only proves uniform marginals for the normalized roots and independence of r_n from the length factor, not mutual independence of the root sequence. For an admissible degenerate cut distribution concentrated at the midpoint, r_{n+1} is a deterministic function of r_n, so the r_n are not independent.

failure_location.quote: we show that all the normalized roots are i.i.d.,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete or replace "i.i.d." with the proven claim, namely that the normalized roots have uniform marginal distributions, and state any independence only where actually proved.
issues.overall_effect: The introduction overstates the proven stochastic structure; the claim of i.i.d. normalized roots is false under the paper's own allowed cut distributions.
issues.title: Overclaim that normalized roots are i.i.d.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: with equality above if and only if $c\in\{0,1\}$ almost surely, and equality below if and only if $c=\frac{1}{2}$ almost surely
The classical bisection algorithm is optimal in the family of stochastic bisection algorithms.

issues.failure_explanation: Since c(1-c) lies in [0,1/4] pointwise, E[c(1-c)] lies in [0,1/4], not [1/2,1]. The equality conditions are also reversed: E[c(1-c)]=0 iff c is in {0,1} a.s., and E[c(1-c)]=1/4 iff c=1/2 a.s. The intended bound is for E[ell]=1-2E[c(1-c)], which lies in [1/2,1].
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the displayed statement to 0 \le E[c(1-c)] \le 1/4, equivalently 1/2 \le E[ell_n] \le 1, with equality E[ell_n]=1/2 iff c=1/2 a.s. and E[ell_n]=1 iff c is in {0,1} a.s.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed inequality is false and does not, as written, support the optimality corollary for the classical bisection method.
issues.title: Incorrect bounds and equality conditions for E[c(1-c)]
issues.why_classification: The correction is a short algebraic fix; the true optimality conclusion survives unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The induction assumes only individual independence of r_n from each past ell_i, and of c_n from each past ell_i. That does not imply that the pair (r_n,c_n), and therefore the function ell_{n+1}, is independent of the past sigma-field. The needed joint independence is not established, so the stated independence argument is incomplete/invalid as written.

failure_location.quote: By the induction hypothesis, we can say the same about $r_n$. Thus, $\ell_{n+1}$ is independent from $\ell_1,\dots,\ell_n$ for all $n>0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the induction to prove joint independence of (r_n,c_n) from the past length factors, or state and prove mutual independence of the ell_n, and then use that in the expectation computation.
issues.overall_effect: The proof does not establish the mutual independence of the ell_n required for E[L_n]=E[ell_1]^n; the corollary is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Invalid induction step in the independence theorem
issues.why_classification: The fix is contained and does not require new global architecture, but it requires a nontrivial joint-independence argument rather than a one-line correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $r_0$ does not have a point mass at $0$ or $1$ (that is, $\mathbb{P}[r_0=0]=\mathbb{P}[r_0=1]=0$) and if the cuts $c_n$ are not almost surely at 0 or 1, then
and similarly for $\lim_{t\to 1} (\mathcal{T}G)(t)$, which implies that $\mathcal{T}$ is continuous at $t=0$ and $t=1$, and thus a positive linear operator from $B_\circ[0,1]$ to $B_\circ[0,1]$.

issues.failure_explanation: The operator argument ignores left limits of discontinuous CDFs. For a CDF G with an atom at c, limits such as G(tc) as t uparrow 1 or G(t+(1-t)c) as t downarrow 0 involve G(c-), not G(c). Consequently T need not map B_circ[0,1] to B_circ[0,1]. A concrete counterexample satisfying the stated hypotheses is r_0=1/2 a.s. and cuts c_n=1/2 a.s.; then the first rescaled root is 1 a.s., so the distribution has a point mass at 1 and remains there, instead of converging uniformly to the uniform CDF.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No source-supported repair preserving the full stated hypotheses is identified; at minimum, the theorem must be restricted to a regularity class (for example continuous CDFs, or CDFs continuous at F-a.e. points so that T preserves B_circ) or a new argument must handle atom-induced endpoint mass.
issues.overall_effect: The central claim that arbitrary endpoint-free initial root distributions converge to the uniform distribution is false as stated, and the downstream general CDF and moment convergence results are unsupported.
issues.title: General convergence theorem false for interior atoms
issues.why_classification: A valid counterexample satisfies the stated hypotheses, and any supported repair either excludes the advertised arbitrary-distribution regime or requires essentially new proof architecture for atomic cases.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Similarly, if $c_n$ are almost surely 1, then $(\mathcal{T}G)(t) = G(1)=1$.

issues.failure_explanation: When c=0 almost surely, t+(1-t)c=t, so (TG)(t)=G(0)+G(t)-G(0)=G(t), not 0. When c=1 almost surely, (TG)(t)=G(t)+G(1)-G(1)=G(t), not 1. The displayed equations are algebraically false, although the intended qualitative conclusion that endpoint-only cuts produce a fixed distribution and hence no convergence to uniform is salvageable.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace both displayed calculations by (TG)(t)=G(t) for c=0 a.s. and c=1 a.s., and then note that a non-uniform fixed CDF does not converge to the uniform CDF.
issues.overall_effect: The digression's displayed necessity argument is incorrect as written.
issues.title: Incorrect operator calculations for degenerate endpoint cuts
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local algebra correction and does not affect the main theorems; the qualitative point survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we find that the cumulative distribution function of $\ell_n$ is

issues.failure_explanation: For arbitrary CDFs, the strict event decomposition omits the atom c_n=r_n, and conditioning on c_n=x gives P[r_n<x]=G_n(x-), not G_n(x), when G_n has an atom at x. Hence the displayed formula is not valid for atomic or mixed distributions. For example, if G_n and F are point masses at 1/2, the formula gives H_n(3/4)=1/2, while ell_n=1/2 a.s. and the true CDF value is H_n(3/4)=1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the formula using left limits and half-open Stieltjes integration (or equivalently state it for the right-continuous CDF with the appropriate endpoint conventions), or restrict the theorem to continuous CDFs.
issues.overall_effect: The general CDF identity and the supremum bound derived from it are not justified for the arbitrary distributions the paper claims to cover; the subsequent general moment convergence corollary is affected.
issues.title: General CDF formula for ell_n ignores atoms
issues.why_classification: The fix is local to the general CDF formula but requires a nontrivial adjustment for atoms and affects downstream general results; it does not by itself change the main continuous-distribution conclusions.
